policy_title: Provide Mental Health Support in Schools
stated: Labour will provide access to specialist mental health professionals in every school, ensuring young people receive early support for mental health problems before they escalate. This initiative will complement the Young Futures Hubs, offering open-access mental health services for children and young people in every community.

source.quote: Poor mental health is another barrier to learning. The struggle to access support is paralysing children and young people through their formative years. Labour will provide access to specialist mental health professionals in every school, so every young person has access to early support to address problems before they escalate. This will complement our plan for Young Futures Hubs, which will make sure every community has an open-access hub for children and young people with drop-in mental health support.

bearing_set.reason: Placing specialist mental health professionals in every school directly affects access to mental health care for young people, a core healthcare-access indicator.
In-school mental health support directly affects educational attainment and opportunity, as untreated mental health problems are a leading driver of the attainment gap and school absence.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: O3 (healthcare access) as the primary designed-for outcome, and O7 (education/opportunity) as a concrete cross-outcome mechanism — mental health is a leading barrier to educational participation and attainment. No other fundamentals reach the non-negligible bar without specific costing evidence for O12 or a concrete liberty/surveillance mechanism for O10.
